A scholar-dragon's library — colossal shelves of ancient leather tomes and rolled scrolls climbing the cavern walls, brass orreries and star-charts on reading-stands, loose parchments drifting underfoot.
A war-dragon's trophy hall — racks of notched swords and shattered shields, the dented armor of slain knights mounted on the walls, tattered banners hanging, a heap of horned skulls in the corner.
A sea-dragon's drowned plunder — barnacled chests and shipwreck-timbers, drifts of pearls and pink coral, rusted anchors and a ship's figurehead, treasure crusted with salt and sea-glass.

A nature-dragon's living hoard — great antlers and bleached bones woven through with blooming vines, chunks of amber glowing with trapped insects, petrified logs and a scatter of gems grown over with moss.

An art-collector dragon's gallery — stolen marble statues lining the walls, rolled tapestries and gilt-framed paintings stacked in careful rows, ceramic masks arranged by expression, a curator's hoard of stolen beauty.

A crystal-dragon's geode chamber — split geodes glowing violet and amber, raw crystal clusters growing from the floor, shelves of sorted gemstones arranged by color, the whole cave humming with refracted light.

A bone-dragon's ossuary — thousands of skulls stacked in neat columns, long bones racked like timber, carved sarcophagi pushed against the walls, funerary masks and grave-goods sorted by civilization and century.

A mage-dragon's relic vault — glowing staves socketed into stone cradles, enchanted orbs floating at eye height, runic tomes chained shut on iron lecterns, shelves of bottled spells flickering with cold fire.

A magpie-dragon's curiosity heap — broken clocks and dented mirrors tumbled together, a sextant beside a music box beside a glass eye, mismatched silverware, tin toys, the gleaming chaos of a jackdaw mind.

A royal hoard — jeweled crowns arranged on velvet-draped pedestals, scepters crossed on the wall, a stolen throne dominating the center, ermine cloaks folded beneath ruby-studded regalia from a dozen fallen dynasties.
A brood-dragon's nest — a great bowl of soft wool and silk, dragon eggs cradled in gold-threaded fabric, warm river-stones piled to hold heat, every treasure chosen for softness over shine.
A minimalist dragon's altar — bare black stone with three objects placed in silence: one cracked mirror, one sealed iron box, one human hand preserved in resin, nothing else, nothing wasted.

A plague-dragon's apothecary hoard — stoppered bottles of dark liquid ranked on shelves, dried herbs bundled and hanging, plague-masks, surgeon's tools, journals of symptoms written in cramped hands, the smell of rot and copper.

A dream-dragon's collection — pale moth wings pinned under glass, stoppered vials of smoke, a library of dream-journals, mirrors that show nothing, hourglasses filled with silver sand, everything soft and quietly wrong.

A music-dragon's archive — lutes and lyres hung from the ceiling, shelves of wax-sealed song-scrolls, a massive pipe organ built into the cave wall, the bones of bards interred lovingly beneath the floor.

A storm-dragon's plunder — shattered ship masts and torn sail-canvas, lightning-struck trees charred to glass, lodestones and compass needles all spinning, a collection of things destroyed mid-motion, frozen at the moment of ruin.

A cartographer-dragon's map vault — every wall papered in overlapping maps, globes in iron cradles, surveying instruments in velvet cases, scrolls of coastlines that no longer exist, a hoard of places more than things.

A judge-dragon's law hoard — stacked law-codes and treaties in sealed clay jars, scales of polished bronze mounted on columns, written confessions, execution orders, contracts signed in blood, the bureaucracy of centuries of judgment.

A classic gold-hoard dragon — mountainous dunes of gold coins and loose gemstones, chalices and chains half-buried, the cliché done to blinding excess, every surface glittering, the weight of it audible in the silence.

A harvester-dragon's seed vault — thousands of ceramic jars sealed with wax, each labeled in tiny script, interspersed with bundled grains, dried flowers, pressed leaves, the patient hoard of a dragon who fears extinction.

A spy-dragon's intelligence cache — coded correspondence pinned to the walls, portraits of nobles with notes scratched in margins, forged seals and stolen signet rings, a hoard of secrets arranged by consequence.

A time-dragon's relic chamber — hourglasses of every size ranked by the year of their making, stopped clocks, calendars from dead civilizations, a collection of things that once measured time now frozen in it.

A feast-dragon's larder — great clay amphorae of salted meat and aged wine, spice jars labeled in twelve languages, exotic preserved fruits, cooking vessels of bronze and silver, a hoard built entirely around appetite.

A forge-dragon's workshop hoard — unfinished blades cooling on iron racks, ingots of rare metal sorted by alloy, bellows and tongs arranged with obsessive care, a collection of metals that haven't yet become what they will.

A grief-dragon's memorial hoard — portraits of the dead arranged on ledges, names carved into the walls, small personal objects — a child's shoe, a wedding ring, a letter — each placed precisely, a hoard of loss kept sacred.
